details: The Trump administration is reportedly preparing to impose higher tariffs on goods from China, the European Union, and 14 other economies, covering an estimated $2.4 trillion in US imports. This move, which could be announced as early as this week, is anticipated to increase inflation and complicate the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions, particularly regarding a potential interest rate hike in December. Following this report, Bitcoin's price fell over 6%, briefly dipping below $60,000, reflecting market concerns over tighter monetary conditions and rising consumer prices.
title: US Prepares New Tariffs, Bitcoin Dips on Inflation & Fed Concerns

details: The European Union has put forth its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, which includes new measures targeting cryptocurrency platforms and international payment networks. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated that approximately 60 Russian banks might be disconnected from the SWIFT system, and a dedicated task force has been established to strengthen efforts against sanctions evasion involving cryptocurrencies. The proposal aims to pressure channels Russia uses to finance its activities in Ukraine and could extend restrictions to financial networks in third countries facilitating sanctions circumvention.
title: EU Proposes New Crypto Sanctions Against Russia

details: South Korea's Financial Services Commission has proposed a draft "Act on Digital Asset Industry Innovation and User Protection." This legislative initiative includes provisions to lift the domestic ban on Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs), which has been in effect since September 2017. The proposal outlines requirements for mandatory white paper disclosures and issuance limits for ICOs. Additionally, it suggests that banks should collectively hold a controlling stake (50% plus one share) in groups responsible for issuing won-pegged stablecoins.
title: South Korea Considers Lifting ICO Ban, Regulating Won Stablecoins
